newsitem.title: HUNGARY: HEAVY-WEIGHTS' LOSSES SLOW DOWN BUX INDEX RISE.
newsitem.headline: HEAVY-WEIGHTS' LOSSES SLOW DOWN BUX INDEX RISE.

text.p: Gainers outnumbered losers on the Budapest Stock Exchange on Thursday but losses by some heavy-weights slowed down the rise of the index, traders said.

The BUX index advanced 26.40 points to end at 3,557.94 points. BUX index futures closed higher for all maturities by 24.50 to 60.00 points, but for December 1997, which remained unchanged at 4,200.00 points.
Traders said foreign investors' purchases focused practically on two issues, pharmaceuticals Richter and chemical firm Borsodchem .
"Foreigners purchased only Richter and Borsodchem and they were selling all other papers," said Robert Agoston of Daewoo Securities.
Traders said recent news of Borsodchem's capacity expansion were encouraging.
Richter, on their opinion, was now cheap and a good long-term investment, although an increased supply was likely as preference shares are expected to appear.
Another pharmaceuticals maker, Human was seen as expensive.
"As for (pharmaceuticals maker) Human domestic small investors pushed its price higher," he said.
Human, extending its recent gains, rose to a new high of 2,740 forints, although later it retreated to end at 2,670 forints, up 70.
Agoston, saying he regarded Human overvalued, explained its recent rise by psychology, rather than based on fundamental news.
Traders said that yesterday's announcement by Humanpharma, member of Human group, and Ciba Hungaria, that they boost their cooperation, is not very significant.

Packaging company Cofinec , which has almost continuously fallen since the release of its disappointing first half results on August 30, rose 13 percent or 520 forints to end at 4,520, still remaining far below its 6,425 forint subscription price.
Agoston said the market was watching out for consumer price inflation figures, to be released tomorrow, after the publication of producer price inflation figures.
